title: SLO aggregation and tenant signal flattening playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic playbook for aggregating SLI metrics and flattening per-tenant signal noise so dashboards and alerts are useful for operators and product teams. Focus: inference-serving metrics (latency, token-cost, cold-cache tail), tracing annotations for multi-hop requests, and dashboard composition patterns that limit query cost while preserving investigatability.

Context and motivation:
- We run inference in a multi-tenant environment where tenant traffic and prompt shapes vary widely. Naively summing or high-cardinal slicing of SLIs leads to noise, alert fatigue, and expensive queries.
- Goal is to provide a compact set of SLI aggregations + probe definitions that:
  1) keep operator-facing alerts stable,
  2) enable tenant-level drilldowns for true incidents,
  3) bound query cost for dashboards and runbooks.

High-level approach:
- Tier signals into three levels: Global (platform health), Cohort (capacity / behavior archetypes), and Tenant (for escalation).
- Flattening strategy: compute coarse cohort signals at ingestion (prometheus recording rules or near-ingest transform) and reserve on-demand tenant rollups for investigation windows only.
- Tracing: attach minimal span annotations to act as keys for rapid correlation (trace_key: request_cohort, tenant_hint, model_variant). Use sampled high-fidelity traces for slow-path investigations.

Definitions (recommended canonical SLI names):
- inference.request.latency.p50 / p95 / p99 : server processing time excluding network egress (ms).
- inference.kv.cache.warmth : fraction of requests that hit in-memory KV on first token (0..1).
- inference.token.cost.unit : billing-normalized token cost per inference (normalized cents).
- inference.request.error.rate : fraction of requests resulting in 5xx or model-fallback responses.
- inference.kv.eviction.rate : evictions/sec per model-shard.
- inference.cold_start.rate : rate of sessions that required model reload or longer-than-expected startup (> threshold ms).
Notes: prefer p95 for operator alerts and p99 for regression detection in CI/rollouts. p50 is useful for UX notes but not for SLOs.

Cohorting heuristic (recording rule guidance):
- request_cohort := coalesce(request_tier, default) + ':' + model_bucket + ':' + length_bucket(prompt_tokens)
  - request_tier = customer_tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - model_bucket = small/medium/large (by parameter/compute class)
  - length_bucket = short/medium/long (> 512 tokens)
- Persist request_cohort at ingestion (low-cardinality). This is the key used for cohort aggregates.

Aggregation rules and recording strategies:
- Compute cohort-level p95/p99 as near-real-time recording rules (1m resolution) using histogram sketches or approximate quantiles to avoid expensive raw aggregation.
- Maintain a rolling 1h window of tenant rollups for tenants over threshold (traffic > X qps or cost > $Y/day). These are retained off-primary dashboards to avoid UI clutter.
- For tenant-level alerts, only create alerts via a templated escalation flow that references cohort baselines. Do not create per-tenant static SLOs unless requested by account escalation.

Tracing annotation pattern (minimal span schema):
- root span tags: trace_key, tenant_id_hash (hashed, not PII), cohort, model_variant, route_id - critical internal spans: kv_lookup, model_infer, prefix_merge, compile_cache_load - span logs: emit tokenized_path_hint (short string), kv_hit boolean, latency_ms - sampling policy: 1% global always-sampled traces; upsample by 10x for requests where p95 latency > threshold or model_fallback==true; 100% sampling for synthetic canary probes and manual debug windows.
Reasoning: keep span width small (few tags) and use a stable trace_key to attach to dashboard drilldowns and support correlation with logs and traces.

Dashboard composition guidelines:
1) Operator home: a single-pane cohort rollup view showing top 10 cohorts by qps with p95, error_rate, and kv_warmth. Each cohort row has a small sparkline and a 1-click drill action that opens a cohort-level investigation notebook (prefilled query).
2) Cost-aware panels: token_cost heatmap binned by model_bucket x length_bucket. Show rolling 24h and 7d deltas.
3) Tenant quickcard: for a given tenant (on-demand), surface: cost last-24h, p95, kv_warmth, recent traces (sample), and top 3 model_variants. This card should be computed by a cached backend API, not by on-the-fly PromQL.
4) Trace anchors: every dashboard panel that shows p99 must include a link to a reproducible trace query with the trace_key for the selected time range.

Query cost and caching rules:
- Prefer recording rules and pre-aggregated tables for p95/p99. Avoid ad-hoc raw-series joins in UI panels.
- Use approximate sketches (t-digest, HDR histograms) and expose precomputed quantiles in widgets.
- Cache tenant quickcards behind a 60s cache and invalidate only when a manual investigation is started or when cohort-level alert fires.

Probes and synthetic checks:
- Simple probe types: end-to-end token generation (E2E), cold-start probe, kv-warmth probe (prefix repeat), model-fallback probe.
- Probe cadence: E2E 1m, kv-warmth 15s for warm-cohort probes, cold-start 10m for low-traffic models.
- Probe tagging: each synthetic probe must include trace_key synthetic:<probe_type>:<region> and be excluded from billing metrics aggregation.

Runbook / escalation pattern (template):
1) Platform alert fires at cohort p95 breach -> ops triage: check cohort quickcard and cohort drill (are multiple tenants affected?).
2) If >1 tenant impacted in cohort -> create incident, route to serving-runtime and infra.
3) If single tenant -> open customer-facing ticket via CS and run tenant rollup.
4) Always attach top 3 traces (p95/p99) and last successful synthetic probe times to the incident.

Maintenance checklist (quarterly):
- Validate cohort definitions against traffic (do we have new model_buckets?).
- Prune cohorts with < 0.1% global qps and archive their recording rules.
- Review sampling rates for traces and adjust up for any increase in model fallbacks.
- Run a dashboard cost audit and remove any panels with query cost > threshold per month unless owner can justify.

Unresolved questions / open TODOs:
- Thresholds: define concrete numeric thresholds for tenant rollup eligibility (cost and qps). Current placeholder: qps > 0.5 or cost > $150/day. Need product ops signoff.
- Privacy: confirm hashing algorithm and retention bounds with security (PII guardrails).
- Tooling: implement a lightweight backend to compute tenant quickcards; engineering estimate needed (ENGOBS-342).

Appendix: Example PromQL snippets (informal)
- cohort_p95: recording rule example (pseudo):
  - record: inference:cohort:latency_p95:1m
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, request_cohort))
- kv_warmth_cohort: sum(rate(inference_kv_hit_total[5m])) by (request_cohort) / sum(rate(inference_request_total[5m])) by (request_cohort)

Notes to self:
- Keep cohort naming short and stable; avoid runtime changes that will re-ingest metrics into new cohorts.
- Tie this doc into the rollout playbook for quantized-model launches (product-hosted-api).

Owner actions (next 2 weeks):
- Get product-ops approval on tenant thresholds (Priya).
- Spin up prototype recording rules for 3 high-volume cohorts (Jonah).
- Draft trace sampling change and run short experiment (Evan).
